title: Manufacturing Devices and Instruments for Easier Rat Liver Transplantation
protocol: Handle: Secure an Nr 10 carbon scalpel blade on a wooden board with tape.
Tag the center of the ring under the microscope.
Drill a 2 mm hole with a spherical diamond bit mounted on a high-speed drill.
Widen the hole using fusiform or conic diamond bits.
Design the shape of the handle with a permanent marker.
Convert the drill into a mini bench grinder and remove the part of the blade outside the shape.
Round off the piece with a low speed rotating brush.
Approximator: Cut off half of one branch under the microscope using the high-speed mini bench grinder.
Make symmetrical grooves on both sides to allow for the handle to slide in completely.
Cut a longitudinal slit in the long arm and check that the center of the long arm and a well-positioned handle are on the same axis.
Design a notch on the long arm facing the center of the handle.
Make the branch as thin as possible.
Round off the piece with the low speed rotating brush.
Cuffs: Design cuff calipers according to the rat weight and strain.
Keep the length of the cuffs around 4 mm.
Take fine-bore polyethylene tubing.
Round off one edge with an Nr 10 scalpel.
Design a grove 0.5 mm from the rounded edge.
Carefully cut out a slope going down to the grove.
Cut out one or two full-thickness nicks into the tubing.
Cut the cuff at 4 mm from its edge.
